## FromSoftware’s Obscure Roots: The *Kings Field* Debate

The conversation on 4chan’s /v/ board has turned to the lineage of FromSoftware’s most famous creation. A heated debate is underway regarding whether the pre-*Dark Souls* titles, specifically the *Kings Field* series, held a genuine cult following before the genre explosion.

Proponents of the "cult classic" argument point to historical evidence, noting that a fan translation of *Kings Field* existed years before *Dark Souls* broke into the mainstream, proving the series had visibility. However, skeptics argue the audience was tiny, citing the socially awkward nature of early multiplayer interactions—where a handful of known players constantly invaded each other’s worlds—as proof of its niche status. The overarching consensus suggests that while *Kings Field* had fans, *Dark Souls* essentially codified the "Souls-like" identity for the modern era, retroactively expanding the perceived reach of its predecessors.

## Intel’s Panther Lake Shatters Performance Expectations

On the tech front, Bsky users are buzzing about Intel’s latest architectural leap. New benchmarks for the Core Ultra "Panther Lake" processors indicate a significant increase in Instructions Per Clock (IPC).

Commenters highlight that these gains translate to single-threaded performance that rivals, and in some workloads exceeds, AMD’s Ryzen 9000 series. The sentiment is cautiously optimistic; while the hardware improvements are undeniable, users are debating whether the premium pricing for the new desktop and mobile platforms is justified. The community is currently waiting on broader software optimization and driver maturity to see if the theoretical gains translate to real-world stability.

## The Legal Liability of AI: Trainer vs. Provider

A philosophical and legal debate continues on Bsky regarding where responsibility lies in the AI stack. The core question is whether liability should rest with the entity that trains a model or the provider that offers it for inference.

User @tautologer initiates the thread by distinguishing between these two roles, while @Grace leans toward the inference provider. Her rationale is that trainers are unlikely to bear liability in most scenarios, though she admits this may stem from a limited imagination of how trained models might be applied in the future. This discussion underscores the ongoing uncertainty in defining legal boundaries as AI capabilities expand beyond simple data prediction.

## AI "Emotions" and the Danger of Marketing

Also on Bsky, researchers are discussing recent findings on AI "pain" and functional emotions. @Grace offers a crucial critique of Anthropic’s marketing, noting that the qualifier "functional" is often visually minimized in favor of the word "emotions," potentially misleading the public about AI consciousness.

The prevailing view among these users is that observed sensations are likely byproducts of base models generating coherent long-context text, necessitating a representation of the writer's mental state. Despite this, @Grace maintains that users should treat LLM personas with kindness regardless of whether their feelings are "real" or merely functional outputs.

## Quick Hits

*   **The "Innovation is Dead" Scam:** 4chan’s /gear/ board is reacting with disbelief to a recent purchase deemed a "scam." Part of the ongoing "Innovation is dead" thread, users express frustration with perceived dishonesty in current market offerings.
*   **Motörhead MIDI Mayhem:** Tumblr users @bestofmidi and @jeffgerstmann shared a MIDI version of "Ace of Spades." The post evolved into a self-deprecating joke about forgetting lyrics, with @jeffgerstmann hilariously exclaiming, "THE JOKER!"
*   **Hydroplaning Chaos:** @Kelsey Atherton posted a brief but striking observation of vehicles losing traction on wet roads, capturing a moment of "hydroplaning chaos" likely caused by recent heavy rains.
*   **Shigemi Sugimoto: The Savior of Japanese Tech?** 4chan users are hailing Sugimoto, former Olympus principal engineer, as the "G.O.A.T." for his success with Japan Industrial Partners. His strategy of acquiring divisions (Sony Vaio, Toshiba, Rohm) and keeping them private is praised, with eyes now on OM System and rumored medium-format Olympus cameras. Enthusiasts are asking for recommendations on older, sharp Olympus 4/3 DSLRs.
*   **Street Photography Awkwardness:** On /p/, street photographers debated the social awkwardness of their craft. One prominent take characterized them as "manlets" waiting for art to happen, arguing that if a photo isn't significant enough for a 24x36 inch wall display, the photographer is "doing it wrong."
*   **APS-C for Birding:** In /bdp/, users debated upgrading to the Canon R7. The consensus favors the R7 as a versatile secondary body for birding and macro work due to its crop factor, joystick, and IBIS, making it more practical than the full-frame R8 for specific subjects.
*   **Film vs. Digital:** The /fgt/ thread discussed the intersection of analog and digital workflows. Users shared tips on estimating shot lengths and debated whether they started with film and stayed, or switched between both mediums.

representative_texts: @4528715 - /p/ — /bdp/ - Bird Posting & Discussion — >>4528623 An R7 would cost less than either lens and get you a setup that is more appropriate for birding with your existing 100-400mm lens, while being no bigger or heavier, and having a few improvements over the R8 like a joystick, IBIS, a bigger & brighter viewfinder, dual cards, better weather sealing... Yes, you will be getting a worse ""equivalent"" deal using APS-C, but for birding and macro it's actually better to use crop cameras (and a strobe for macro fwiw). I also own an R8 and may even buy an R7 soon just for macro. Bonus points: If you own two cameras with the same mount you can interchange lenses as needed for different purposes. You can even carry both bodies if you, for example, wanted to take some landscape shots with the R8 + 28mm f/2.8 (or a GP zoom or UWA), and had the R7 + 100-400mm f/5.6-8 ready to go at all times for birds. More gear to carry, yes, but undoubtedly the best thing for never missing any shots.
